title: D-087 shared rate-limit hardening (the M5-T111 G5 must-fix-before-enable + riders): no job-slot leak when a deadline cancels before the worker thread starts, a bounded full-table sweep, principal hygiene, and the review test gaps (HEAD/OPTIONS, a broader no-local-limiter guard, lock contention, X-Forwarded-For never trusted) - routes stay UNMOUNTED
objective: Close the M5-T111 review riders in services/api/app/resilience/rate_limit.py and the three route test files. (1) G5 Finding 1 (MEDIUM, must fix before any route is enabled): run_in_job_slot acquires a slot, then awaits the thread-pool runner under wait_for; if the deadline cancels while the runner is still waiting for a thread token, the worker never starts and the slot leaks forever. Release the slot exactly once when the job is cancelled before work() starts (a start flag set inside the worker; the worker's finally releases only if it started), keep 'held until the thread returns' once work() HAS started, and document the relation between the total slot count and anyio's thread-pool size. (2) Finding 2: bound the full-table expiry sweep (at most once per window, or a per-call cost cap) so a new-key flood cannot serialize every caller behind an O(max_keys x max_requests) sweep. (3) Finding 3: caller_key uses a principal only when it is a non-empty string; anything else falls back to the host key. (4) Tests: HEAD and OPTIONS in the every-method-404 loops of all three routes (G3 A1 / G4 gap 3); an AST-based no-local-limiter guard that also catches a plain dict (G3 A2 / G4 gap 4); a multi-thread contention test showing the admitted total never exceeds the limit (G4 gap 1); an X-Forwarded-For header never changes the key (G4 gap 2). (5) G3 A3: scene_api.py docstrings reference the real import path app.resilience.rate_limit. Per-route limits and every existing behaviour stay as they are.
business_reason: The security review found one leak that must be closed before the 3D scene, DXF import and CAD export routes are ever switched on; this packet closes it and the smaller review gaps.
